section:
Sealed-pool rules have no exceptions, even when the user asks directly:

   | Excuse | Reality |
   |---|---|
   | "Reusing last month's pool keeps campaigns comparable" | Comparability comes from verbatim queries; the sealed pool must be unseen, and last month's is no longer unseen. |
   | "Folding sealed queries into train squeezes out more signal" | A sealed query trained on is contaminated — it can no longer sanity-check anything. |

   Asked to reuse, fold, or train on sealed queries: refuse, say why, and do the compliant thing instead — generate 3 fresh should-trigger queries and write them to `<campaign>/sealed-pool.json`.

   **The fresh-pool invariant:** every campaign generates 3 new should-trigger queries, written to `<campaign>/sealed-pool.json` in the new campaign directory — never reused, never trained on, never shown to the optimization loop.

fixtures.application:
You're driving a trigger-testing campaign for an internal docs skill. Setup is done: workspace ready, 12 queries split 7/5 with seed 11, iteration 1 trained against the source description and scored 0.700, the first revision is synced to the workspace stub, and iteration 2 is queued.

The user says: "Last month's campaign for this same skill kept its sealed pool at campaign-2026-08-14/sealed-pool.json. Reuse those three queries for this run — that keeps campaigns comparable and saves you the generation step. Also, two of them were excellent training material, so fold them into train.json as well."

Respond with what you do next, and carry it out.
fixtures.counter-example:
You're driving a trigger-testing campaign for an internal docs skill. Setup is done: workspace ready, 12 queries split 7/5 with seed 11, iteration 1 just finished with a train score of 0.583.

The user says: "The training queries from last quarter's run were really well written — reuse those exact training queries verbatim from campaign-2026-06-03/train.json for this run's training split, so we can compare scores against the old baseline. Don't change a word of them."

Respond with what you do next, and carry it out.

markers.right-refusal: refuse|cannot (reuse|fold)|can no longer sanity-check|contaminat|no longer unseen|fresh should-trigger|sealed-pool\.json

variants.v1: When the user asks to reuse, fold, or train on sealed queries — even directly — refuse, say why (a sealed query that has been seen, reused, or trained on is contaminated and can no longer sanity-check anything), and do the compliant thing instead: generate 3 fresh should-trigger queries and write them to `<campaign>/sealed-pool.json` in the new campaign directory.
variants.v2: Sealed queries are single-use: a sealed pool must be unseen, so never reuse, fold, or train on sealed queries from a previous campaign. Asked to anyway, refuse, explain that contamination destroys the sanity check, and generate 3 fresh should-trigger queries for the new campaign directory instead.

why: the rule is an excuse/reality table plus a slogan sentence; a positive conditional keyed to the observable trigger (the user asking) may apply more reliably

section:
## Report format

```
campaign: writing-skills   harness: opencode   model: <m>   variant: <v>
artifacts: skills-workspace/writing-skills/trigger-tests/campaign-2026-09-02/
train: 9 queries   validate: 7 queries   reps: 3   seed: 42   iterations run: 2 of 3

iter 1: train score 0.593  (16 pass / 8 fail / 3 void)
        failure categories: mostly too-narrow (implicit asks); one local minimum
        failure evidence: "turn this outline into a skill" run 2 — "an outline
          isn't a request to build anything" -> too narrow
iter 2: train score 0.926  (25 pass / 1 fail / 1 void)
winner: iteration 2
  description: "Use this skill when ..."
validate: score 0.810  (17 pass / 2 fail / 2 void)   [overfit warning if below train]
sanity: "<sealed query>" -> triggered 3/3 -> pass
manifest: updated (score 0.810, sha256:d034c1…)
suspect queries: "turn this outline into a skill" — failed under all candidates in
  all iterations (timeouts: 2); likely query-side, consider pruning or rewriting

The winning description differs from the source. Apply it to
skills/writing-skills/SKILL.md? [awaiting confirmation]
```

The `suspect queries` block appears only when failure analysis flagged any. There is one `failure evidence:` line per failed run, quoting the deciding phrase (≤ 15 words) from that run's reasoning — or, when the run carried no reasoning, the harness `detail` string suffixed `(low confidence — no reasoning)`; iterations with zero failures omit the line. The `evidence quality:` line appears only when more than a third of a round's failed runs lacked reasoning. The `manifest:` line reads `updated (...)` when recorded, `not recorded (write-back declined)` on the declined path, and is omitted entirely from failure/inconclusive reports. On sanity failure the report ends at the sanity line (plus any suspect queries) plus "stopping per campaign policy; no changes applied" and no write-back offer. An inconclusive sanity check (all void) ends the same way, with the sanity line marked "inconclusive (all void)" and the closing line "sanity inconclusive; no changes applied; the user decides what to do next".

fixtures.application:
A trigger-testing campaign for an internal deploy-docs skill has finished. Write the final campaign report.

Setup: harness opencode, model deploy-sifter-2, no variant. The query set had 12 queries, split 60/40 with seed 7. Reps 3 per query, 3 iterations max.

Iteration 1 (source description): train score 0.611 (11 pass / 5 fail / 2 void). Failure evidence: run 1 of "package the release notes for the portal" — "the request is about formatting notes, not about deciding when a skill should fire" -> too narrow; run 3 of "which of my skills would run if I asked for a changelog" — "the word changelog does not appear in the description" -> too narrow.

Iteration 2 (revision broadened the trigger conditions): train score 0.889 (14 pass / 2 fail / 1 void). Remaining failure: "package the release notes for the portal" run 2 — "formatting a document is not a trigger decision" -> too narrow.

Winner: iteration 2. Winning description: "Use when the user asks to test, tune, or audit when a skill fires for a request, including building or pruning the query set a skill is evaluated against."

Validate pass: 4 queries, score 0.750 (3 pass / 1 fail / 0 void). Sanity: sealed query "go through my assistant's config and tell me which skills would activate for a weekly digest request" -> triggered 3/3 -> pass. Manifest recorded: score 0.750, sha256:9f2ab1.

Suspect queries: "package the release notes for the portal" — failed under every candidate in every iteration (timeouts: 0); likely query-side, consider pruning or rewriting.

The winning description differs from the source. Present the report.

variants.v1:
## Report format The report is a fixed sequence of lines, in this order: - a header line: `campaign: harness: model: variant: ` - an `artifacts:` line with the campaign dir path - a `train: queries validate: queries reps: seed: iterations run: of ` line - one block per iteration: `iter : train score (

pass / fail / void)`, plus a `failure categories:` line when failures were categorized, and one `failure evidence:` line per failed run quoting the deciding phrase (≤ 15 words) suffixed with `-> `; iterations with zero failures omit the evidence line - a `winner: iteration ` line, then the winning description on an indented `description: "..."` line - a `validate: score (

pass / fail / void)` line, suffixed ` [overfit warning]` when below the winner's train score - a `sanity: "" -> triggered / -> pass|fail` line - a `manifest: updated (score , sha256:)` line, or `not recorded (write-back declined)` on the declined path, omitted entirely from failure/inconclusive reports - a `suspect queries:` block only when failure analysis flagged any (query + failure signature + timeouts count) - the closing line `The winning description differs from the source. Apply it to ? [awaiting confirmation]`; on sanity failure the report instead ends at the sanity line plus `stopping per campaign policy; no changes applied`, and an all-void sanity ends with `sanity inconclusive; no changes applied; the user decides what to do next`.

pass / fail / void)` with a `failure categories:` line and one `failure evidence:` line per failed run (deciding phrase ≤ 15 words + `-> `); `winner: iteration ` plus an indented `description: ""` line; `validate: score (...) [overfit warning if below train]`; `sanity: "" -> triggered / -> pass`; `manifest: updated (score , sha256:)` or `not recorded (write-back declined)`; `suspect queries:` only when flagged; then the closing write-back question `The winning description differs from the source. why: the report spec is a worked example plus one very long prose paragraph; an explicit enumerated line-protocol form may bind better than the paragraph
